    The core innovation of GPM is to treat prior initialization    Contemporary Vision–Language–Action (VLA) models
as a memory-driven retrieval problem rather than a ﬁxed            typically divided into two categories: single-stream archi-
noise design. It consists of three components: a Prior Head        tectures [14, 15, 25, 32, 48] and hierarchical architectures
that integrates current multimodal information; a Memory           [1, 7, 12, 16, 31]. Single-stream architectures employ a vi-
Bank that stores and retrieves task-level priors; and a Prior-     sion–language backbone and autoregressively generate dis-
Aware Sampler for prior action distribution sampling to-           cretized action tokens [11, 13]. To meet the high-frequency
gether with adaptive noise scale and NFE. By initializing          control demands of real-world scenarios, various efﬁciency
the generative ﬂow in the neighborhood of similar tasks,           techniques, such as parallel decoding [15, 34], parameter
GPM drastically narrows the prior-target gap. This not only        quantization [39], and token compression [17, 18], have
reduce the required NFE but, critically, anchors the pro-          been adopted to increase inference speed. On the other
cess in feasible action space. Adaptive noise injection re-        hand, hierarchical approaches contain a vision–language
tains the model’s exploratory power, preventing determinis-        backbone for high-level, low-frequency planning, a gen-
tic collapse and preserving generalization to novel tasks.         erative policy [6, 44] for low-level, high-frequency ac-

Figure 2. Overview of OptimusVLA framework. Given a task and the current observation, the Vision–Language backbone ﬁrst encodes
the inputs into a multimodal representation. GPM then retrieves a task-level prior based on this representation, while LBM dynamically
encodes the historical action sequence to produce a consistency constraint. Finally, the ﬂow policy denoises the initialization with an
adaptive NFEs schedule to generate the action chunk.

pare the inference time and NFEs of OptimusVLA against                                                  In this paper, we propose a dual-memory VLA framework,
π0.5 on simulation benchmark and Real-World. Opti-                                                      OptimusVLA, which contain Global Prior Memory (GPM)
musVLA achieves 6.5× faster inference time and 3.1×                                                     and Local Consistency Memory (LCM) for robotic manip-
fewer NFEs on LIBERO, while simultaneously delivering                                                   ulation. GPM replaces Gaussian noise with task-level pri-
the highest task performance. We attribute these gains to the                                           ors retrieved from semantically similar trajectories, thereby
lightweight design of GPM and LCM, which introduce min-                                                 shortening the generative path and reducing invalid samples
imal overhead yet substantially reduce the required NFEs.                                               without sacriﬁcing generalization. LCM models short his-
                                                                                                        tories of executed actions to infer task progress and injects
